thread:
alex.price: Heads-up: after yesterday's KMS rewrap there are signs that API key scope enforcement is asymmetric for embeddings vs chat routes. filing here before we escalate.
marta.li: 😬 noticed earlier when running smoke tests — embeddings endpoints returned results with a token that should only have `embeddings:read` while chat calls were blocked. can repro locally.
sam.green: ok can you paste the minimal repro and any logs? did the token get reissued or is it an old token pre-rotate?
alex.price: old token issued pre-rotation. repro steps:
```
# embeddings succeeds
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $OLD_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
# chat fails
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $OLD_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
logs show 403 for chat with this code in auth-proxy:
```
authz.check: route=chat model=gpt-open v=2 scopes_required=[chat:generate] token_scopes=[embeddings:read] -> DENY
```
marta.li: interesting part: the token metadata in KMS audit shows it still had `allowlist: ["/v1/embeddings"]` in the key tag after rewrap. but the route-level checker uses per-route scope mapping from the new RBAC table which maps `model:open` -> `chat:generate` + `embeddings:read`. so mismatch.
jen_ops: could be two separate issues: (A) scope tags on wrapped keys weren't preserved for legacy tokens, (B) authz service uses an old mapping cache or reversed precedence between explicit per-route allowlists and model-derived scopes.
sam.green: I pulled the auth-proxy trace. The flow is: token -> token_service (verifies signature & KMS tag) -> scope_builder (merge allowlist + model-scopes) -> authorizer. Repro trace shows scope_builder returned only `embeddings:read` for the token. stack shows `allowlist` win over `model_scopes` because of a recent refactor to prefer explicit tags.
alex.price: But we intended model_scopes to be additive; the refactor accidentally made allowlist override and drop model scopes for legacy tokens. that seems to explain why chat is denied.
rotation-bot: INFO: rewrap job 2026-03-19T02:12Z completed for key-id:kk-xxxx, metadata_preserved=false
marta.li: oh that bot message explains a lot — metadata_preserved=false. KMS rewrap path didn't reapply our custom tags when creating the new wrapped key. so tokens that rely on key tags for implicit scopes lost those tags.
jen_ops: action plan proposal:
  - short term: add a backwards-compatible fix in authz: when model_scopes are missing, consult the model->scope mapping and add those scopes rather than dropping them. can ship a hotfix behind a quick toggle.
  - mid term: update rotation job to preserve key tags (`metadata_preserved=true`) and add a migration to re-tag newly wrapped keys with the expected allowlists.
  - add regression e2e that uses pre-rotate tokens against chat + embeddings endpoints.
sam.green: agree. also: add an audit alert when `metadata_preserved=false` for any production rewrap so SRE/security get paged.
alex.price: who wants to own the hotfix and the KMS job change?
jen_ops: I can take hotfix (authz patch + toggle). expecting ~2-3 hours to validate and roll as canary.
marta.li: i'll own the rotation job change & migration, will need a db migration to map old tag schema to new, and a runbook to rewrap any keys missing tags.
sam.green: i'll add the e2e regression and an automated smoke check post-rotation in our CI that fails if chat != embeddings scope parity.
rotation-bot: TODO: create incident ticket INC-2026-042 (linked)
alex.price: thanks all. please add short notes to the incident ticket about blast radius: observed for ~7 customer tokens in prod (limited to internal staging earlier). recommend notifying customers with affected tokens and offer forced reissue.
jen_ops: for customer communication — let's not call it a data breach; it's an authorization mismatch. prepare a templated note: what happened, who was impacted (tokens that used pre-rotation tags), mitigation steps, ETA for permanent fix.
marta.li: discovered two flaky test cases in CI that masked this: they generated tokens via new-token path which had explicit scopes embedded (so they passed). i've added a test that simulates legacy pre-rotate tokens.
sam.green: quick checklist for rollout:
  1) branch with authz hotfix behind toggle
  2) canary to 5% traffic for 30m
  3) flip toggle for all auth-proxies
  4) deploy rotation job fix & rewrap migration (run during low-traffic window)
  5) post-migration smoke check (our new e2e)
jen_ops: will send ping in #all-hands for the low-traffic window; prefer Thu 03:00 UTC.
alex.price: 👍 also add logs to ensure we can trace back: token_id -> wrapped_key_id -> rewrap_job_id. we lost that chain in the current audit output.
rotation-bot: NOTE: scheduled rewrap migration job candidate window Thu 03:00 UTC
marta.li: i'll attach a log sample to the incident later. for now, going to start the authz patch PR.
alex.price: thanks. assigning follow-ups in incident ticket. keep updates short here. :eyes:
